title: Drowning, Diving and Altitude: Water, Pressure and Thin Air

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already open airways, ventilate with a BVM, do CPR and decide on spinal motion restriction. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Manage drowning as a lung problem, and choose PEEP or CPAP
  2. Use the pressure laws to tell squeeze, air embolism and the bends apart
  3. Recognize altitude illness: AMS, HAPE and HACE

Textbook: Chapter 38, PDF pages 3288–3314
slides.say: Welcome to the second half of Chapter 38: water, pressure and thin air. As EMRs, you already manage the airway, ventilate with a bag-valve mask, do CPR, and decide on spinal motion restriction. As a PCP, you get new airway tools, PEEP and CPAP, and new decisions about who should and shouldn't get them. Drowning is our main focus, because you'll see it most. Then we'll use three simple gas laws to understand diving injuries, and finish with altitude illness. In every case, the real problem is the same: getting oxygen into the patient.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第三十八章的后半部分：水、压力和稀薄空气。作为 EMR，你们已经会管理气道、用球囊面罩通气、做 CPR，并判断是否需要脊柱运动限制。作为 PCP，你多了新的气道工具 PEEP 和 CPAP，也多了新的决定：谁该用、谁不该用。溺水是重点，因为你最常遇到。然后用三条简单的气体定律理解潜水损伤，最后讲高原病。每一种情况，真正的问题都一样：把氧气送进病人体内。

slides.title: Drowning: a continuum
slides.body:
Drowning = breathing impaired by submersion in liquid

breath-hold→laryngospasm→hypoxia, CO₂ rises→water in stiff lungs→arrest
  • "Near drowning" is no longer used
  • 10–15% die in laryngospasm, with dry lungs
  • Salt or fresh water: no difference in your care
  • You can rescue the patient at any point
slides.say: Since 2002, drowning has a simple definition: breathing problems caused by being submerged in a liquid. Drowning is a continuum. The person holds their breath, then water touches the airway and the vocal cords clamp shut. That's laryngospasm. Oxygen falls and carbon dioxide builds up; about ten to fifteen percent die here, with dry lungs. Usually the larynx relaxes, water enters, and the lungs become stiff and frothy. Then the heart stops. Salt or fresh water makes no real difference to your care. The key message: it's a breathing problem, and you can rescue the patient at any point.
slides.sayZh: 从二零零二年起，溺水有了简单的定义：因浸没在液体中而导致的呼吸障碍。溺水是一个连续过程：先屏气，然后水碰到气道，声带猛地关闭，这叫喉痉挛。氧气下降、二氧化碳积聚，约百分之十到十五的人死在这一阶段，肺里是干的。多数情况下喉部会松开，水进入肺，肺变硬、出现泡沫，接着心跳停止。咸水还是淡水，对你的处理没有实际区别。关键是：这是呼吸问题，在任何一个阶段都有机会救回来。

slides.title: Drowning: airway first
slides.body:
• Leave water rescue to trained teams; wear a flotation device
  • No routine SMR: only for diving, water slides, obvious trauma, alcohol
  • No abdominal thrusts to "drain" the lungs
  • Ventilate early: hypoxia is the problem
  • Expect vomiting: suction ready, protect the airway
  • BC asphyxial arrest, alone with an AED: 5 cycles of CPR first
slides.say: Leave water rescue to trained teams, and wear a flotation device near the water. Once you have the patient, the airway comes first. Spinal motion restriction isn't routine; use it for diving, water slides, obvious injuries, or when alcohol was involved. Never use abdominal thrusts to drain the lungs; they push stomach water into the lungs. Ventilate early. Expect vomiting: about two thirds vomited with rescue breaths and eighty-six percent with compressions. And because drowning is an asphyxial arrest, BC says that if you're alone with an AED, do five cycles of CPR, about two minutes, before applying it.
slides.sayZh: 水中救援交给受过训练的团队，靠近水边要穿漂浮装置。病人到手后，气道优先。脊柱运动限制不是常规，只用于跳水、玩滑水道、有明显外伤或涉及饮酒的情况。绝不要用腹部冲击把肺里的水「挤出来」，那会把胃里的水压进肺里。尽早通气。要预料到呕吐：约三分之二的人在人工呼吸时呕吐，按压时则有百分之八十六。因为溺水属于窒息性骤停，BC 规定如果你一个人带着 AED，先做五个循环、约两分钟的 CPR，再贴 AED。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the BC drowning protocol
slides.body:
BC Drowning/Near Drowning protocol and CPAP guidelines

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • SMR if the mechanism calls for it
  • Keep at rest; position sitting up
  • Remove wet clothes, dry, keep warm
  • Avoid rough handling
  • Basic airway; IPPV if breathing is failing
  • Arrest: resuscitate per the guideline

PCP adds

  • PEEP or CPAP if indicated
  • CPAP guideline lists submersion injuries
  • PEEP valve on the BVM: start at 5 cmH₂O
slides.say: Here is the BC drowning protocol, and it shows exactly what's new for you. On the left is what you already do as an EMR: spinal motion restriction if the mechanism calls for it, rest, sitting up, wet clothing off, dry and warm, gentle handling, basic airway care, and positive pressure ventilation if breathing is failing. On the right is the PCP addition, a single line but a powerful one: PEEP or CPAP if indicated. The BC CPAP guideline even lists submersion injuries as an indication. Let's see how to choose between them.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的溺水流程，它清楚地显示了你多了什么。左栏是你作为 EMR 已经在做的：按受伤机制需要做脊柱运动限制、让病人休息、坐起、脱掉湿衣服、擦干保暖、轻柔搬动、基本气道处理，呼吸衰竭时给正压通气。右栏是 PCP 多做的，只有一行，但很有分量：必要时用 PEEP 或 CPAP。BC 的 CPAP 指南甚至把淹溺伤列为适应证。下面看怎么在两者之间选择。

slides.title: PEEP or CPAP after drowning?
slides.body:
Both keep alveoli open at the end of each breath and push fluid back out of them.

CPAP (patient breathes)BVM + PEEP (you breathe)
Age ≥ 13, awake, follows commandsBreathing failing, or LOC decreased
RR > 24, SpO₂ < 94% on O₂, accessory muscles8–10 breaths per minute
5 cmH₂O, up by 2.5 to max 105 cmH₂O, up by 2.5 to max 10
Not if vomiting, LOC down, SBP < 90, traumaRemove if SBP < 90 or arrest
slides.say: Why does positive pressure help after drowning? PEEP and CPAP keep some pressure in the lungs at the end of each breath, holding the alveoli open and pushing fluid back out. Choose by how the patient is breathing. CPAP is for a patient who breathes on their own: thirteen or older, awake, breathing faster than twenty-four, saturation below ninety-four on oxygen, using accessory muscles. Never with vomiting, a decreased level of consciousness, a systolic under ninety, or trauma. If breathing is failing, you breathe for them with a bag-valve mask and a PEEP valve, and remove it if the systolic falls below ninety.
slides.sayZh: 为什么正压对溺水有帮助？PEEP 和 CPAP 在每次呼吸末保留一点压力，撑开肺泡、把液体推回去。按病人的呼吸状态来选。CPAP 用于能自主呼吸的病人：十三岁以上、清醒、呼吸快于每分钟二十四次、吸氧下血氧低于九十四、动用辅助呼吸肌。有呕吐、意识下降、收缩压低于九十或创伤时绝不能用。如果呼吸衰竭，就由你用球囊面罩加 PEEP 阀替他呼吸；收缩压降到九十以下就取下 PEEP 阀。

slides.q: A 17-year-old was pulled from a lake. He is awake and following commands, RR 32, SpO₂ 89% on a non-rebreather, using accessory muscles, BP 124/78. He has vomited twice and is still retching. You are the PCP. What about CPAP?
options: Start CPAP at 5 cmH₂O: submersion injury is an indication
No CPAP: active vomiting is a contraindication; O₂, suction, and BVM + PEEP if he tires
Start CPAP at 10 cmH₂O to clear the water faster
Use abdominal thrusts first, then start CPAP
slides.say: Let's make a PCP decision. A seventeen-year-old was pulled from a lake. He's awake and following commands, breathing thirty-two times a minute, saturation eighty-nine percent on a non-rebreather, using accessory muscles. His blood pressure is one hundred twenty-four over seventy-eight. He has vomited twice and is still retching. What about CPAP? A, start CPAP at five, because submersion injury is an indication. B, no CPAP, because active vomiting is a contraindication; give oxygen, have suction ready, and use a bag-valve mask with PEEP if he tires. C, start CPAP at ten to clear the water faster. D, use abdominal thrusts first, then start CPAP. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一个 PCP 决定。一名十七岁男孩被从湖里救上来。他清醒、能听从指令，呼吸每分钟三十二次，非重复呼吸面罩下血氧八十九，动用辅助呼吸肌，血压一百二十四比七十八。他已经吐了两次，还在干呕。CPAP 怎么办？A 从五开始上 CPAP，因为淹溺伤是适应证；B 不用 CPAP，因为正在呕吐是禁忌：给氧、备好吸引，他撑不住时用球囊面罩加 PEEP；C 直接从十开始上 CPAP，把水更快清出来；D 先做腹部冲击，再上 CPAP。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. He meets most of the CPAP criteria, but vomiting or any other risk of aspiration is a BC contraindication. A ignores the contraindication. C is wrong because CPAP starts at five and rises in steps of two point five. D is wrong because abdominal thrusts push stomach water into the lungs.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。他符合大部分 CPAP 标准，但呕吐或任何其他误吸风险是 BC 的禁忌。A 忽略了禁忌；C 错在 CPAP 从五开始，每次加二点五；D 错在腹部冲击会把胃里的水压进肺里。

slides.title: After the rescue: everyone goes
slides.body:
• Transport every drowning patient, even if they look fine
  • Lungs can fail hours later: ARDS, pneumonia; kidneys too
  • Under water < 5 min: 85% do well; > 10 min: only 4%
  • Icy water, especially children: keep going (recovery after > 1 h)
  • Take a core temperature; add the hypothermia protocol
  • Wheeze is common; the book uses salbutamol
slides.say: After the rescue, transport every drowning patient, even one who seems fully recovered. Hours or days later, the lungs can fail with ARDS, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or pneumonia. Time under water predicts the outcome: under five minutes, about eighty-five percent do well; over ten minutes, only about four percent. But icy water changes things, especially for children. Full recovery has been reported after more than an hour, so keep resuscitating, take a core temperature, and use the hypothermia protocol too. Wheezing is common; the book uses salbutamol, which is on the BC drug list for EMRs and PCPs.
slides.sayZh: 救上来以后，所有溺水病人都要送医，即使看起来完全恢复了。几小时甚至几天后，肺可能因急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ARDS）或肺炎而衰竭。在水下的时间最能预测结局：五分钟以内，约百分之八十五预后好；超过十分钟，只有约百分之四。但冰水会改变情况，尤其是儿童：有在冰水中超过一小时后完全恢复的报道，所以要坚持复苏，测核心体温，并同时使用低体温流程。喘鸣很常见，原书用沙丁胺醇，它在 BC 药物表里，EMR 和 PCP 都可以用。

slides.title: Diving: pressure and three gas laws
slides.body:
Every 33 feet (about 10 m) of seawater adds 1 atmosphere

DepthPressureGas volume
Surface1 ATA1
33 ft2 ATA½
66 ft3 ATA⅓
  • Boyle: pressure up, gas volume down; on ascent, gas expands
  • Henry: more pressure, more gas dissolves (nitrogen → the bends)
  • Dalton: each gas adds its own pressure (nitrogen narcosis)
slides.say: At the surface we live under one atmosphere, and every thirty-three feet, about ten metres, of sea water adds another. Tissues are mostly water and don't compress, but gas spaces do: lungs, sinuses, middle ears and gut. Boyle's law: as pressure rises, gas volume falls, and as the diver rises, gas expands. Henry's law: more pressure dissolves more gas in the blood, like the gas in a sealed soft drink; open it fast, and bubbles appear. That's the bends. Dalton's law: each gas in a mix adds its own pressure, which explains nitrogen narcosis.
slides.sayZh: 在水面我们承受一个大气压，海水每深三十三英尺（约十米）就再加一个。组织大多是水，不会被压缩，但含气的腔隙会：肺、鼻窦、中耳和肠道。波义耳定律：压力升高，气体体积变小；潜水员上浮时，气体膨胀。亨利定律：压力越大，溶进血液的气体越多，就像密封汽水里的气；猛地打开，气泡就冒出来，这就是减压病。道尔顿定律：混合气体中每种气体各自贡献分压，这解释了氮麻醉。

slides.title: Going down and staying deep
slides.body:
• Squeeze (barotrauma): a gas space can't equalize on descent
  • Middle ear: severe pain; burst eardrum → vertigo, vomiting, panic
  • Ear bleeding: loose dressing only
  • Nitrogen narcosis from ~100 ft: euphoria, poor judgment
  • The fix for narcosis: a controlled ascent
  • Danger: panic → rapid ascent → the worst injuries
slides.say: Going down, the problem is squeeze, or barotrauma: a gas space that can't equalize with the rising pressure outside. A diver who can't clear their ears gets severe ear pain, and if the eardrum bursts, vertigo and vomiting under water. For ear bleeding, use only a loose dressing. From about one hundred feet, nitrogen starts acting like a drug. This is nitrogen narcosis: the diver feels euphoric, laughs, and stops caring about safety, a bit like being drunk. The fix is a controlled ascent. The real danger is panic, because a rapid ascent causes the worst injuries.
slides.sayZh: 下潜时的问题是「挤压」，也就是气压伤：某个含气腔隙无法和外面不断升高的压力平衡。潜水员耳朵平衡不了，就会剧烈耳痛；如果鼓膜破了，会在水下出现眩晕和呕吐。耳朵出血只用松松的敷料。大约一百英尺开始，氮气会像药物一样起作用，这叫氮麻醉：潜水员感到欣快、发笑、不再在乎安全，有点像喝醉。解决办法是有控制地上浮。真正的危险是惊慌，因为快速上浮造成的损伤最严重。

slides.title: Coming up: burst lung and air embolism
slides.body:
• Breath held on ascent → lungs over-expand (POPS, "burst lung")
  • The last 2 m is enough; asthma and COPD raise the risk
  • Air under the neck skin crackles; hoarse voice, chest pain
  • Pneumothorax: unequal breath sounds, low SpO₂, low BP
  • AGE: bubbles reach the brain, usually within 10 min

Unconscious right after a dive = air embolism until proven otherwise.
slides.say: Coming up, gas expands. Lungs filled at thirty-three feet would double in volume at the surface, so divers breathe out all the way up. If they panic and hold their breath, even over the last two metres, alveoli can burst. This is pulmonary overpressurization syndrome, or burst lung. Air can leak under the skin of the neck or into the chest, causing a hoarse voice, chest pain or a pneumothorax. The worst result is arterial gas embolism, or AGE: bubbles reach the brain, usually within ten minutes, causing weakness, seizures or unresponsiveness. A diver who loses consciousness right after surfacing has an air embolism until proven otherwise.
slides.sayZh: 上浮时气体膨胀。在三十三英尺吸满的肺，到水面体积会翻倍，所以潜水员上浮全程都要呼气。如果惊慌屏气，哪怕只在最后两米，肺泡也可能破裂，这叫肺过度膨胀综合征，俗称「爆肺」。空气可能漏到颈部皮下，也可能进入胸腔，引起声音嘶哑、胸痛或气胸。最严重的后果是动脉气体栓塞（AGE）：气泡进入大脑，通常在十分钟内出现无力、抽搐或无反应。潜水员一出水就失去意识，在排除之前都按气体栓塞处理。

slides.title: Decompression sickness vs air embolism
slides.body:
AGEDCS ("the bends")
Causeburst alveoli → air bubblesnitrogen bubbles out of the tissues
Onsetseconds to minutes; usually < 10 minusually < 1 h; almost always by 6 h
Main signsbrain: LOC, stroke-likejoints (type I); spinal cord, organs (type II)

Both: 100% O₂ by non-rebreather, IV, monitor, fastest route to a hyperbaric chamber (ground preferred).
slides.say: Decompression sickness, or the bends, is Henry's law in action. At depth, extra nitrogen dissolves in the tissues; if the diver comes up too fast, it bubbles out. Symptoms usually start within an hour and almost always within six. Type one affects the skin and joints, and joint pain is the most common symptom. Type two affects the spinal cord and other organs, and it's more serious. On scene you often can't tell it from an air embolism, and you don't need to: give one hundred percent oxygen and get the patient to a hyperbaric chamber by the fastest route.
slides.sayZh: 减压病，俗称「潜水病」，就是亨利定律在起作用。在深处，多余的氮溶进组织；如果潜水员上浮太快，氮就以气泡形式冒出来。症状通常在一小时内出现，几乎都在六小时以内。一型累及皮肤和关节，关节痛是最常见的症状；二型累及脊髓和其他器官，更严重。现场你常常分不清它和气体栓塞，也不需要分清：给百分之百氧气，用最快的方式把病人送到高压氧舱。

slides.q: A diver ran out of air and shot to the surface. Three minutes later she is confused, with weakness in her right arm. What is the best plan?
options: Entonox for comfort, then the nearest emergency department
100% oxygen by non-rebreather and the fastest route to a hyperbaric chamber
Observe for 6 hours to see whether decompression sickness develops
BVM ventilation with PEEP at 10 cmH₂O to push the air back
slides.say: Here's a diving case. A diver ran out of air and shot to the surface. Three minutes later she's confused, with weakness in her right arm. What's the best plan? A, Entonox for comfort, then the nearest emergency department. B, one hundred percent oxygen by non-rebreather mask, and the fastest route to a hyperbaric chamber. C, observe her for six hours to see whether decompression sickness develops. D, bag-valve mask ventilation with PEEP at ten, to push the air back. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来看一个潜水病例。一名潜水员气瓶没气了，急速冲出水面。三分钟后她意识混乱，右臂无力。最好的方案是什么？A 给笑气让她舒服一点，然后送最近的急诊；B 非重复呼吸面罩给百分之百氧气，用最快的方式送往高压氧舱；C 观察六小时，看会不会出现减压病；D 用球囊面罩加十的 PEEP 通气，把空气推回去。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Stroke-like signs within minutes of a rapid ascent mean an arterial gas embolism until proven otherwise. She needs one hundred percent oxygen and recompression in a hyperbaric chamber as fast as possible. A is wrong because Entonox is contraindicated in BC for air embolism, decompression sickness and pneumothorax. C wastes time she doesn't have. D is wrong because the book warns against PEEP in burst lung, and she is breathing on her own.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。急速上浮后几分钟内出现类似卒中的表现，在排除之前都按动脉气体栓塞处理。她需要百分之百氧气，并尽快在高压氧舱里加压治疗。A 错在 BC 规定气体栓塞、减压病和气胸禁用笑气；C 浪费了她没有的时间；D 错在原书警告爆肺时不能用 PEEP，而且她能自主呼吸。

slides.title: Altitude illness: AMS, HAPE, HACE
slides.body:
• Fast climb, usually above 2,500 m (can start at 2,000 m); onset 6–10 h
  • Thin air: less oxygen pressure; fitness doesn't protect
IllnessKey signs
AMSheadache + fatigue, nausea, dizziness or poor sleep
HAPE (lungs)breathless at rest, cough, crackles, cyanosis
HACE (brain)confusion and/or ataxia; can lead to coma

Treatment: oxygen, descent, evacuation.
slides.say: Finally, altitude. The air still has twenty-one percent oxygen, but the pressure is lower, so less oxygen reaches the blood. Illness usually follows a fast climb above two thousand five hundred metres, sometimes from two thousand, within six to ten hours. Fitness doesn't protect; a previous episode is the biggest risk. Acute mountain sickness, AMS, always includes a headache, plus fatigue, nausea, dizziness or poor sleep. High-altitude pulmonary edema, HAPE, is fluid in the lungs: breathlessness at rest, cough, crackles and cyanosis. High-altitude cerebral edema, HACE, is brain swelling: confusion or a staggering walk, called ataxia. Treatment is oxygen, descent, and evacuation.
slides.sayZh: 最后讲高原。空气里仍有百分之二十一的氧，但气压低，进入血液的氧就少。发病通常在快速升到两千五百米以上之后，有时两千米就会发生，多在六到十小时内出现。身体好不能防病，既往发作过是最大的危险因素。急性高山病（AMS）一定有头痛，再加乏力、恶心、头晕或睡不好之一。高原肺水肿（HAPE）是肺里有液体：静息时也气促、咳嗽、湿啰音和发绀。高原脑水肿（HACE）是脑肿胀：意识混乱或走路摇晃，叫共济失调。治疗是给氧、下撤和后送。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• CPAP: not if vomiting, LOC down, SBP < 90, age ≤ 12, trauma
  • CPAP also not with a suspected pneumothorax
  • PEEP off if SBP < 90 or arrest; book: no PEEP in burst lung
  • Entonox: never for DCS, air embolism or pneumothorax (BC)
  • Cold water: core temperature, then the hypothermia protocol
  • Diver? Get depth, bottom time, dives, computer, stops
slides.say: Here are the new traps for a PCP. CPAP has hard stops: vomiting, a decreased level of consciousness, a systolic under ninety, age twelve or under, trauma, and a suspected pneumothorax. PEEP comes off if the systolic drops below ninety or the patient arrests, and the book warns against PEEP when a diver may have burst a lung. Entonox, which you used as an EMR, is contraindicated in BC for decompression sickness, air embolism and pneumothorax, so a diver in pain is not an Entonox patient. And with any diver, take a full dive history, because it changes your plan.
slides.sayZh: 下面是 PCP 要注意的新陷阱。CPAP 有硬禁忌：呕吐、意识下降、收缩压低于九十、十二岁及以下、创伤，以及怀疑气胸。收缩压降到九十以下或病人骤停时，要取下 PEEP 阀；原书还警告，潜水员可能爆肺时不能用 PEEP。笑气是你当 EMR 时就用过的，但 BC 规定减压病、气体栓塞和气胸禁用，所以疼痛的潜水员不是用笑气的对象。遇到任何潜水员，都要问完整的潜水史，因为它会改变你的方案。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: simple CPAP not for drowning → BC: PEEP or CPAP if indicated
  • BC CPAP guideline lists submersion injuries
  • Asphyxial arrest, alone with an AED: 5 cycles of CPR first
  • Book: needle decompression for POPS → not in EMR/PCP scope
  • Book: dopamine, benzodiazepines, lidocaine, acetazolamide → not BC
  • BC epinephrine: IM only
slides.say: For the BC exam, a few differences. The book says simple CPAP devices shouldn't be used after drowning, but the BC drowning protocol says PEEP or CPAP if indicated, and the BC CPAP guideline lists submersion injuries, so follow BC, with its contraindications. For an asphyxial arrest, if you're alone with an AED, do five cycles of CPR first. The book mentions needle decompression for a pneumothorax after burst lung; that's outside EMR and PCP scope in BC. And the book's drugs, such as dopamine, benzodiazepines, lidocaine and acetazolamide, aren't on the BC list. In BC, epinephrine is given by IM injection only.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要注意几点不同。原书说溺水后不应使用简易 CPAP 装置，但 BC 溺水流程写的是必要时用 PEEP 或 CPAP，BC 的 CPAP 指南也列出了淹溺伤，所以按 BC 来，同时遵守它的禁忌。窒息性骤停时，如果你一个人带着 AED，先做五个循环的 CPR。原书提到爆肺后气胸可做针刺减压，这在 BC 不属于 EMR 和 PCP 的范围。原书里的多巴胺、苯二氮卓类、利多卡因和乙酰唑胺等药都不在 BC 药物表里。在 BC，肾上腺素只能肌注。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Drowning = hypoxia: ventilate early, expect vomiting, transport all
  2. PCP adds PEEP or CPAP: know the criteria and the hard stops
  3. Diver in trouble: 100% O₂, hyperbaric chamber, no Entonox

Next: Chapter 39, Infectious and Communicable Diseases
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: drowning is a breathing problem. Ventilate early, never use abdominal thrusts, expect vomiting, and transport every patient, even those who look fine. Two: as a PCP you add PEEP or CPAP. CPAP is for the awake patient who meets the criteria, never with vomiting, a decreased level of consciousness or a low blood pressure. Three: a diver who gets sick after surfacing needs one hundred percent oxygen and a hyperbaric chamber, and no Entonox. Next time we start Chapter 39, infectious and communicable diseases. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 最后记住三件事。一，溺水是呼吸问题：尽早通气，绝不做腹部冲击，预料到呕吐，所有病人都送医，即使看起来没事。二，作为 PCP 你多了 PEEP 和 CPAP：CPAP 用于符合标准的清醒病人，有呕吐、意识下降或低血压时绝不能用。三，出水后发病的潜水员需要百分之百氧气和高压氧舱，不能用笑气。下节课开始第三十九章：感染性和传染性疾病。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
